_comment: Full Census national state data. Each state's LICENSE TERM is what makes its page genuinely distinct (not spun duplicate content) — states use different words for the same small care home, and families search the local word. status: 'live' = terminology verified, page indexed. 'draft' = generated with noindex until Henos confirms the license term, regulator, and count with the state agency. count = number of SMALL homes (the ICP), only rendered when count_verified is true.

states.name: Washington
states.regulator: DSHS Aging and Long-Term Support Administration (ALTSA)
states.blurb: Where Full Census started. My own family's home, Serene Lynnwood, was the first site I ever built — a family found it in week one.

guides.title: How to start an adult family home in Washington
Placement agencies vs. listing your own beds

roster.name: DSHS AFH Locator
roster.fmt: CSV/Excel export from the search UI
roster.notes: Also on geo.wa.gov as 'DSHS Adult Family Homes'. PRA request for emails sent 2026-08-27.

states.name: California
states.term: Residential Care Facility for the Elderly
states.regulator: California Department of Social Services, Community Care Licensing Division
states.search_term: board and care home near me
states.blurb: The biggest small-home market in the country. Families here say "board and care" — most operators' websites say "RCFE," which is one reason families can't find them.

roster.name: CDSS Community Care Licensing facilities (open data)
roster.notes: Filter facility type 740 (Residential Care Elderly) / 741. Also ccld.dss.ca.gov/carefacilitysearch with JSON/CSV export. No records request needed for the spine.

states.name: Wisconsin
states.regulator: Wisconsin DHS Division of Quality Assurance
states.blurb: Wisconsin uses the same words Washington does — adult family home — so everything we built for WA operators translates directly. Larger homes here are licensed as CBRFs.

roster.name: WI DHS Division of Quality Assurance provider directory
roster.notes: AFH (3-4 bed) and CBRF are separate license types — pull both.

states.name: Oregon
states.blurb: Next door to our home state, and the closest market to Washington in both licensing structure and family expectations.

roster.name: ODHS licensed facility directory
roster.notes: Adult foster homes are county-administered in places; expect per-county files.

states.name: Michigan
states.regulator: Michigan LARA, Adult Foster Care Licensing
states.blurb: One of the largest small-home populations in the Midwest, licensed as adult foster care.

roster.name: Michigan LARA adult foster care facility search
roster.notes: AFC small group homes are the ICP; screen out large group homes.

states.name: Georgia
states.regulator: Georgia Department of Community Health, Healthcare Facility Regulation Division
states.blurb: Georgia families search "personal care home" — a completely different phrase from the one operators' own websites usually use.

roster.name: Georgia DCH Healthcare Facility Regulation directory
roster.notes: Personal care homes; separate list from assisted living communities.

states.name: Pennsylvania
states.blurb: Pennsylvania licenses small homes as personal care homes, separate from its larger assisted living residences.

roster.name: PA DHS personal care home directory

states.name: Texas
states.term: Assisted Living Facility, Type A or Type B
states.beds: Type B covers residents needing more assistance
states.regulator: Texas Health and Human Services Commission
states.blurb: Texas splits small homes into Type A and Type B licenses — and the residential assisted living investor wave has created thousands of new owner-operators who have never marketed anything.

roster.name: Texas HHSC long-term care provider search
roster.notes: Type A vs Type B matters for the pitch; Type B homes serve higher-acuity residents.

states.name: North Carolina
states.regulator: NC Division of Health Service Regulation
states.blurb: North Carolina's family care home license covers exactly the 2–6 bed homes we serve best.

roster.name: NC DHSR facility lists
roster.notes: DHSR publishes clean per-type lists; family care homes are their own category.

states.name: Arizona
states.blurb: Arizona's assisted living home license is built for the small residential model, and the retiree population keeps demand high year-round.

roster.name: AZDHS licensed facility search
roster.notes: Assisted living homes (<=10 beds) are separate from assisted living centers.

states.name: Florida
states.beds: up to 5 residents in the provider's own home
states.regulator: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA)
states.blurb: Florida licenses the small home as an adult family care home — the operator lives in the house, exactly like a Washington AFH. Larger properties are licensed as ALFs.

roster.name: Florida AHCA / FloridaHealthFinder
roster.notes: Adult Family Care Home (AFCH) is the small-home license, separate from ALF. AHCA data is among the cleanest in the country.
